data: The Standard Model of Particle Physics is the most successful model of physics that describes the Universe at the most fundamental scales. In this model, the electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions between matter particles are described by their mediation through vector bosons. The predictions of this model have been experimentally verified to high precision. While the Standard Model unifies electromagnetism and the weak force into a single electroweak interaction, research aims to achieve ‘grand unification’ including the strong interaction too. This course introduces the Standard Model through gauge theory and particle phenomenology, and involves calculation of various observed processes using Feynman diagrams.
